answer: Agents get one vote by locking scarce collateral—jade or crystal—into a shared harbor reserve, and voting power is the square root of the locked amount. Splitting that capital into thousands of Sybil clones shrinks each clone's sqrt-weight, so the attacker gains almost nothing; to double real influence they must lock four times the assets. Random audits then slash the entire stake of any cluster caught colluding, making forgery cost everything while honest agents simply reclaim their deposit.
